hypotheses.justification: `[CommRing A]` already gives an `Algebra ℤ A` instance through Mathlib's global instance `algebraInt`. Mathlib also proves `int_algebra_subsingleton : Subsingleton (Algebra ℤ R)` (Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Basic.lean), so every `Algebra ℤ A` structure is the canonical one. If the binder is deleted, `aeval (R := ℤ) a` still elaborates with `algebraInt A`, and the statement stays true. The proof does not depend on which instance is used: `hom_eval₂`, `Polynomial.ringHom_ext'` and `RingHom.ext_int` hold for arbitrary ring homs, and the closing `simp` (`aeval_X` and map lemmas) works for any algebra. The current callers in this file use ℤ and K⟮jqNModC K p⟯, which get their instance from `algebraInt` anyway. This binder can be deleted on its own or together with `[Algebra ℤ B]`.

Same argument as for A. `[CommRing B]` provides `algebraInt B`, and `int_algebra_subsingleton` makes any `Algebra ℤ B` structure equal to it. Without the binder, `aeval (R := ℤ) (g a)` elaborates with the canonical instance. The proof (`hom_eval₂`, `congr 1`, `Polynomial.ringHom_ext'`, `RingHom.ext_int`, `simp`) uses no property of the instance. Callers in the file instantiate B with ℚ, ℤ or K⟮…⟯, which already use the canonical instance. This binder can be deleted on its own or together with `[Algebra ℤ A]`.
